Gelman is a Bayesian who spends a lot of time on how Bayesian analyses go wrong. These eleven entries follow a model from its foundations to its checks, in roughly the order you meet the ideas when you start.

## Part 1: Probability and priors

1. **[Probability](../concepts/probability.qmd).** A long-run frequency and a degree of belief, learning from the same coin.
2. **[Bayesian](../concepts/bayesian.qmd).** Gelman's joke about Bayesians, and what a confident prior in the wrong place does.
3. **[Weakly Informative Priors](../concepts/weakly-informative-priors.qmd).** What to use when you think you want a noninformative prior.
4. **[What were you doing before you had any data?](../concepts/before-you-had-any-data.qmd).** Simulate from your prior and see whether you believe the data it implies.
5. **[The Bayesian cringe](../concepts/bayesian-cringe.qmd).** There is no need to apologize for using what the field already knows.

## Part 2: The rest of the model

6. **[Camel that is the likelihood](../concepts/camel-likelihood.qmd).** The data model usually matters more than the prior everyone argues about.
7. **[Multiple Comparisons](../concepts/multiple-comparisons.qmd).** Partial pooling instead of corrections: the multilevel model as the everyday Bayesian tool.
8. **[Bayesians](../concepts/bayesians-are-frequentists.qmd).** Bayesian intervals have a frequency property too, averaged over the prior.

## Part 3: Computing and checking

9. **[The Folk Theorem of Statistical Computing](../concepts/folk-theorem.qmd).** When the sampler struggles, look at the model first.
10. **[A chicken](../concepts/a-chicken.qmd).** Check a model by its inferences: an implication that makes no sense points to a flaw.
11. **[Uncertainty Interval](../concepts/uncertainty-interval.qmd).** Say this instead of confidence or credible interval; in most problems they cover alike.
